summary: Mr. Mosseri explains the Halabi custom of the Swenee, where a groom sends three trays to his bride-to-be before she goes to the mikveh prior to marriage. He explains the meaning of the word Swenee, the connection to the three mentions of ve'erastikh from Hoshea, and what was carried on each of the three trays. He also describes how items such as 101 coins, baylun clay, ka'ak bi-loz, habbat al-baraka, and henna were used by the women at the mikveh.

questions: What does the word Swenee mean and where does it come from?
Why did the groom in Halab send three trays to the bride before the mikveh?
How do the three trays connect to tefillin and the pesukim of Hoshea?
What items were sent on each of the three trays?
Why were habbat al-baraka and henna thrown into the mikveh water?
